# SB-1047: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev B

Hazard description
The induction power cabinet for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) has presented an increased arc flash risk during recent maintenance and troubleshooting operations. The most likely initiating conditions are energized conductive dust accumulation at cabinet terminations, degraded insulation on control wiring, and inadequate coil cooling water flow leading to localized overheating at the coil joints and power cabling. An arc flash event in this cabinet can produce intense light, heat, and blast forces that will cause severe injury to personnel and damage to surrounding equipment. The event pathway frequently involves energized work on or near the main incoming and outgoing power connections, control contactors, and coil terminations.

Background and step rationale
During routine review of operational incidents and preventative maintenance feedback following ECN-2026-010 and SB-1044, engineering and safety teams identified recurring contributors to cabinet arc events at hot induction systems. The induction coil thermal stability and the integrity of the power cabinet environment are primary risk drivers. Maintaining the coil cooling water flow at the specified minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is critical to prevent coil hot spots that increase fault current potential at connections and accelerates insulation degradation. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min.

Other preventive factors include strict cabinet cleanliness, verified insulation resistance on power and control wiring, and enforced procedures for de-energizing and verifying absence of voltage prior to any exposed conductive work. The steps in the required controls are chosen to remove power, control the work boundary, and ensure cooling and cabinet condition are within design assumptions before any intervention.

Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet serving Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03), plant P3, line P3-L1.
- Associated induction coil cooling loop feeding EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Incoming feeder and outgoing power terminations, control contactors and local control wiring within the cabinet.
- Any portable diagnostic equipment used at the cabinet for live testing.

Required controls
1. Cooling verification
- Before any energized work or start-up following any maintenance that opens the cooling circuit, confirm coil cooling water flow meets the specified minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03): 65 L/min. Do not proceed if the flow is below that specified minimum.

2. De-energize and verify
- All work on exposed conductors or terminations requires de-energizing in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-05. Verify absence of voltage using approved test instruments rated for the system before beginning work. Follow lockout/tagout procedures exactly as required by site practices.

3. Work boundary and PPE
- Establish a controlled work boundary around the cabinet for any intervention. Only authorized personnel who have completed site-specific arc flash training are permitted inside the boundary. Appropriate arc-rated PPE must be selected based on the task analysis performed using the methods in SB-1044 and documented in the task hazard assessment.

4. Housekeeping and contamination control
- Implement routine cabinet cleaning and inspection to remove conductive dust and debris. Ensure enclosure seals and filters are functional to reduce ingress of dust and coolant deposits that can form conductive paths.

5. Insulation and connection integrity
- Inspect and verify the condition of power connectors, coil terminations, and control wiring insulation prior to re-energization. Tighten terminations and replace degraded insulation only while de-energized. Any repair that could alter connection impedance or thermal profile must include verification of coil cooling flow at the specified minimum prior to commissioning.

6. Procedures for live diagnostics
- Live diagnostics are restricted to activities that cannot be completed de-energized and require a documented technical justification signed by engineering. Live work must follow the controls in SOP-P3-L1-05 and include insulated barriers, remote test probes, and a dedicated safety observer.

7. Incident response
- If any abnormal heating, burning smell, arcing, or visible damage is observed, immediately de-energize the cabinet and isolate the coil cooling loop. Initiate incident reporting as described in ECN-2026-010 and commence root cause analysis with engineering and safety.

Examples and application notes
- Example: If a technician must replace a control module inside the cabinet, the module replacement is to be performed only after de-energizing and verifying absence of voltage in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-05. After reassembly, verify coil cooling water flow for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 meets 65 L/min prior to re-energizing to ensure the coil thermal environment returns to safe operating conditions.
- Example: If troubleshooting requires measuring under-load conditions, prepare a documented live work permit that references the task hazard assessment and specifies use of remote probes and a safety observer. Limit live exposure time and stage partial energization only as necessary for measurement, with immediate de-energize plans in place.

Records to keep
- Maintain a work permit or job brief for every intervention in the cabinet area and retain it in the maintenance record system associated with EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Record coil cooling water flow verification with the exact value recorded and associated instrument used. The verification must be attached to the maintenance or startup checklist for the cabinet.
- Keep inspection and cleaning logs for the power cabinet, including findings on insulation condition and termination integrity.
- Archive incident reports, root cause analyses, and corrective action plans in the document control system and link to ECN-2026-010 when applicable.

Effective date
Effective immediately. All personnel assigned to work on or near EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must review this bulletin and applicable procedures, including SOP-P3-L1-05 and SB-1044, and apply the controls described herein before the next work activity. Compliance will be verified by engineering and safety during subsequent planned maintenance and follow-up audits.
